newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: US surge sees Australian stocks open higher.
newsitem.headline: US surge sees Australian stocks open higher.

text.p: Australian shares opened higher on Wednesday as investors took inspiration from Wall Street's return to its record-breaking run and pushed the local market higher.
Shortly after the opening, the All Ordinaries index climbed 16.8 points to 2,382.8.
Aided by a bounce in base metals prices and an oversold situation on Tuesday, brokers said the opening spell had seen the market regain some lost ground.
"It's been on the back of better commodity prices and I think it was a bit overdone yesterday," said broker Tony Russell of Morgan Stockbroking.
"The confidence was back in Wall Street. It was expected to be a weaker day on Wall Street but it surprised on the upside and we are picking up the gains we lost yesterday."
Local inspiration was largely lacking with the major corporate event likely to be the release of ANZ Bank's full year profit results, due later today.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about 11 to four, while 44 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
